problem: Transformer-based VLN agents (e.g. PTA) lag behind LSTM-based ones on R2R, and speaker-based back-translation trains the speaker separately from the follower. Most strong methods also rely on pre-exploration or beam search, which is impractical for real robots.
motivation: Domestic service robots need to follow language instructions in a single run, without building an exhaustive map first. Transformers can train faster on long sequences and exploit pretrained language models, but their VLN potential is under-explored. Sharing latent features between follower and speaker may improve both.
key_idea: A cross-modal transformer follower (CMT) with cross-modal path masking, trained jointly with a transformer speaker (CMS) that shares latent action features, so paths are translated into instructions and generated instructions are translated back into paths (double back-translation).
insight: The ablations show that both path masking and DBT help. On val-unseen, CMT-type1 (neither) reaches SR 0.48 / NE 5.44, CMT-type2 (masking, no DBT) reaches 0.50 / 5.01, and the full CMT reaches 0.55 / 4.60. Filtering generated data (successful paths for the speaker, SPICE > λ for sentences) limits noise from the augmentation. SPL stays low, probably because there is no RL objective penalizing path length.
method: Inputs and single-run setting: instruction, 36 panoramic views at the current node, adjacent edges and previous actions; only local graph knowledge, with no pre-exploration or beam search.
Language encoder: MiniLM (384-d) embeddings plus a 2-layer transformer with self-attention and cross-modal attention to the current visual features; the CLS token gives h_l.
Visual encoder: ResNet-152 features concatenated with Matterport semantic views and relative azimuth/elevation encodings; cross-modal attention conditioned on language; the CLS token gives h_v.

Action decoder: 2-layer causal transformer over previous action embeddings; the second layer takes o_a concatenated with context C=h_l⊕h_v. Scores are dot products with candidate actions, trained with cross-entropy and sampling.
Cross-modal path masking: BERT-like random masking of ground-truth actions, predicted causally; used in pre-training.
CrossMap Speaker: 2-layer transformer that generates instructions from the shared latent action features o_a, using causal and bidirectional masking.

Double back-translation: the CMS is trained on CMT paths that reach the goal; the CMS then labels ground-truth and unlabeled paths (~170k Speaker-Follower paths), keeping only sentences with SPICE > λ=20, to train the CMT.

setting.backbone: CrossMap Transformer (2-layer transformers, MiniLM embeddings, ResNet-152 features), trained from scratch apart from MiniLM

results: On R2R val-unseen, CMT reaches SR 0.55, NE 4.60, SPL 0.44, OSR 0.63 in the single-run setting. This is well above the transformer baseline PTA (SR 0.43) and comparable to the LSTM-based PREVALENT (0.58) and CMG-AAL (0.59), though SPL is lower. On val-seen it reaches SR 0.73 and NE 2.82, on par with CMG-AAL and with the best OSR (0.80). The CMS is better than the baselines only on SPICE (21.9).
limitations: SPL is lower than the best LSTM methods because there is no RL or shortest-path optimization; SR does not exceed PREVALENT or CMG-AAL on val-unseen.
The speaker is weaker on BLEU, CIDEr and ROUGE than the Speaker-Follower baseline, and only SPICE is favorable.
Evaluated only on R2R in simulation, with no real-robot experiments.
